302	                  WORKING_DIRECTORY ${ESP_HAL_3RDPARTY_FETCH_SOURCE_DIR})
303	  execute_process(COMMAND git apply --directory components/mbedtls/mbedtls nuttx/patches/components/mbedtls/mbedtls/0002-mbedtls_add_prefix_to_macro.patch
304	                  WORKING_DIRECTORY ${ESP_HAL_3RDPARTY_FETCH_SOURCE_DIR})

306	  if(NXTMPDIR AND NOT EXISTS "${ESP_HAL_3RDPARTY_CHIP_DIR}")

319	  if(CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_WIRELESS)

323	      COMMAND
324	        git submodule --quiet update --init --depth=1 components/esp_phy/lib

326	        components/bt/controller/lib_esp32c6/esp32c6-bt-lib
327	        components/bt/controller/lib_esp32h2/esp32h2-bt-lib
328	        components/esp_coex/lib

243	/* Response Encodings:
244	 *
245	 * xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxD OSMT TTRR RRCC CCCC
246	 *
247	 * x - Bit not used
248	 * C - Bits 0-5:   Command index
249	 * R - Bits 6-9:   Response type
250	 * T - Bits 10-12: Data transfer type
251	 * M - Bit 13:     MMC Multiblock transfer
252	 * S - Bit 14:     Stop data transfer
253	 * O - Bit 15:     Open drain
254	 * D - But 16:     SDIO Multiblock transfer
255	 */
256	
257	#define MMCSD_RESPONSE_SHIFT (6)
258	#define MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK  (15 << MMCSD_RESPONSE_SHIFT)
259	#  define MMCSD_NO_RESPONSE  (0)
260	#  define MMCSD_R1_RESPONSE  (1 << MMCSD_RESPONSE_SHIFT) /* 48-bit */
261	#  define MMCSD_R1B_RESPONSE (2 << MMCSD_RESPONSE_SHIFT) /* 48-bit */
262	#  define MMCSD_R2_RESPONSE  (3 << MMCSD_RESPONSE_SHIFT) /* 128-bit */
263	#  define MMCSD_R3_RESPONSE  (4 << MMCSD_RESPONSE_SHIFT) /* 48-bit */
264	#  define MMCSD_R4_RESPONSE  (5 << MMCSD_RESPONSE_SHIFT) /* 48-bit */
265	#  define MMCSD_R5_RESPONSE  (6 << MMCSD_RESPONSE_SHIFT) /* 48-bit */

267	#  define MMCSD_R7_RESPONSE  (8 << MMCSD_RESPONSE_SHIFT) /* 48-bit */

717	/****************************************************************************
718	 * Name: SDIO_WAITENABLE
719	 *
720	 * Description:
721	 *   Enable/disable of a set of SDIO wait events.  This is part of the
722	 *   the SDIO_WAITEVENT sequence.  The set of to-be-waited-for events is
723	 *   configured before calling either calling SDIO_DMARECVSETUP,
724	 *   SDIO_DMASENDSETUP, or SDIO_WAITEVENT.  This is the recommended
725	 *   ordering:
726	 *
727	 *     SDIO_WAITENABLE:    Discard any pending interrupts, enable event(s)
728	 *                         of interest
729	 *     SDIO_DMARECVSETUP/
730	 *     SDIO_DMASENDSETUP:  Setup the logic that will trigger the event the
731	 *                         event(s) of interest
732	 *     SDIO_WAITEVENT:     Wait for the event of interest (which might
733	 *                         already have occurred)
734	 *
735	 *   This sequence should eliminate race conditions between the command/
736	 *   transfer setup and the subsequent events.
737	 *
738	 *   The enabled events persist until either (1) SDIO_WAITENABLE is called
739	 *   again specifying a different set of wait events, or (2) SDIO_EVENTWAIT
740	 *   returns.
741	 *
742	 * Input Parameters:
743	 *   dev      - An instance of the SDIO device interface
744	 *   eventset - A bitset of events to enable or disable (see SDIOWAIT_*
745	 *              definitions). 0=disable; 1=enable.
746	 *   timeout  - Maximum time in milliseconds to wait.  Zero means immediate
747	 *              timeout with no wait.  The timeout value is ignored if
748	 *              SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT is not included in the waited-for eventset.
749	 *
750	 * Returned Value:
751	 *   None
752	 *
753	 ****************************************************************************/
754	
755	#define SDIO_WAITENABLE(dev,eventset,timeout) ((dev)->waitenable(dev,eventset,timeout))
756

763	 *   returns.  SDIO_WAITEVENTS must be called again before SDIO_EVENTWAIT
764	 *   can be used again.
765	 *
766	 * Input Parameters:
767	 *   dev - An instance of the SDIO device interface
768	 *
769	 * Returned Value:

133	#define SDMMC_CTRL_AUTOSTOP              (1 << 10) /* Bit 10: Send STOP after CCSD to CE-ATA device */
134	#define SDMMC_CTRL_CEATAINT              (1 << 11) /* Bit 11: CE-ATA device interrupts enabled */

509	config ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_ENABLED
510		bool "Enable Flash Encryption on boot (READ DOCS FIRST)"
511		default n
512		depends on ESPRESSIF_BOOTLOADER_MCUBOOT
513		select ESPRESSIF_EFUSE
514		---help---
515			If this option is set, flash contents will be encrypted by the bootloader on first boot.
516	
517			Note: After first boot, the system will be permanently encrypted. Re-flashing an encrypted
518			system is complicated and not always possible.
519	
520			Read https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/security/flash-encryption.html
521			before enabling.
522	
523			Note: enabling this option will automatically select ESPRESSIF_EFUSE and ESPRESSIF_EFUSE_VIRTUAL,
524			as a mean to avoid accidental burning of the E-Fuses.
525	
526	if ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_ENABLED
527	
528	config ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_UART_BOOTLOADER_ALLOW_ENC
529		bool "Leave UART bootloader encryption enabled"
530		depends on ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENCRYPTION_MODE_DEVELOPMENT
531		default n
532		---help---
533			If not set (default), the bootloader will permanently disable UART bootloader encryption access on
534			first boot. If set, the UART bootloader will still be able to access hardware encryption.
535	
536			It is recommended to only set this option in testing environments.
537	
538	config ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_UART_BOOTLOADER_ALLOW_DEC
539		bool "Leave UART bootloader decryption enabled"
540		default n
541		depends on ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENCRYPTION_MODE_DEVELOPMENT
542		---help---
543			If not set (default), the bootloader will permanently disable UART bootloader decryption access on
544			first boot. If set, the UART bootloader will still be able to access hardware decryption.
545	
546			Only set this option in testing environments. Setting this option allows complete bypass of flash
547			encryption.
548	
549	config ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_UART_BOOTLOADER_ALLOW_CACHE
550		bool "Leave UART bootloader flash cache enabled"
551		default n
552		depends on ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENCRYPTION_MODE_DEVELOPMENT
553		---help---
554			If not set (default), the bootloader will permanently disable UART bootloader flash cache access on
555			first boot. If set, the UART bootloader will still be able to access the flash cache.
556	
557			Only set this option in testing environments.
558	
559	choice ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENCRYPTION_MODE
560		bool "Enable usage mode"
561		default ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENCRYPTION_MODE_DEVELOPMENT
562		---help---
563			By default, Development mode is enabled which allows ROM download mode to perform Flash Encryption
564			operations (plaintext is sent to the device, and it encrypts it internally and writes ciphertext
565			to flash). This mode is not secure, it's possible for an attacker to write their own chosen plaintext
566			to flash.
567	
568			Release mode should always be selected for production or manufacturing. Once enabled it's no longer
569			possible for the device in ROM Download Mode to use the Flash Encryption hardware.
570	
571			Refer to the Flash Encryption section of the ESP-IDF Programmer's Guide for details:
572			https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32/security/flash-encryption.html#flash-encryption-configuration
573	
574	config ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENCRYPTION_MODE_DEVELOPMENT
575		bool "Development (NOT SECURE)"
576		select ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_UART_BOOTLOADER_ALLOW_ENC
577	
578	config ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENCRYPTION_MODE_RELEASE
579		bool "Release"
580	
581	endchoice
582	
583	config ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_USE_HOST_KEY
584		bool "Require user provided encryption key for flash encryption"
585		default y
586		---help---
587			This option enables the requirement of a host generated flash encryption key.
588	
589			If not selected, a random key will be generated by the bootloader on first boot.
590			In this case, the user will not have access to the key and will be unable to reuse it.
591	
592	if ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_USE_HOST_KEY
593	
594	config ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_HOST_KEY_NAME
595		string "Path to flash encryption key"
596		default "flash_enc_key.bin"
597		---help---
598			Path to the key file used to encrypt the flash.
599	
600			This key is in a binary format and is generated by espsecure application.
601	
602			Path is evaluated relative to the NuttX root directory.
603	
604			You can generate a new signing key by running the following command:
605			$ espsecure.py generate_flash_encryption_key <key_name>
606	
607	endif # ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_USE_HOST_KEY
608	
609	config ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_FLASH_DEVICE_ENCRYPTED
610		bool "Device is already encrypted"
611		default n
612		depends on ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENCRYPTION_MODE_DEVELOPMENT
613		depends on !ESPRESSIF_EFUSE_VIRTUAL
614		---help---
615			Append --encrypt to esptool.py write_flash command.
616	
617			This option is useful when the device already has a flash encryption key,
618			and the user wants to simply flash a new firmware to it, using the key already present.
619			It requires that the DEVELOPMENT mode is set. It is not possible to reflash in RELEASE mode.
620	
621	endif # ESPRESSIF_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_ENABLED

2674	menu "Ethernet Configuration"
2675		depends on ESPRESSIF_EMAC
2676	
2677	config ESPRESSIF_ETH_NRXDESC
2678		int "RX descriptor number"
2679		default 20
2680		---help---
2681			Number of DMA receive descriptors/buffers used by the EMAC.
2682			Each buffer is CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_ETH_DMA_BUFFER_SIZE bytes.
2683			The default of 20 provides headroom for TCP-style ACK bursts
2684			that arrive while the upper layer is busy submitting a TX burst
2685			(otherwise the EMAC asserts RX_BUFF_UNAVAILABLE and silently
2686			drops incoming frames, forcing TCP retransmissions).
2687	
2688	config ESPRESSIF_ETH_NTXDESC
2689		int "TX descriptor number"
2690		default 20
2691		---help---
2692			Number of DMA transmit descriptors/buffers used by the EMAC.
2693			With CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_ETH_DMA_BUFFER_SIZE=1600, each descriptor
2694			holds one Ethernet frame.  TCP send() bursts up to ~12 segments
2695			back-to-back; 20 descriptors gives ample headroom so that
2696			esp_eth_transmit() never returns ESP_ERR_NO_MEM mid-burst.
2697			If the ring is exhausted, frames are silently dropped and
2698			retransmissions happen via fast-retransmit/RTO, drastically
2699			degrading throughput.
2700	
2701	config ESPRESSIF_ETH_DMA_BUFFER_SIZE
2702		int "DMA buffer size (bytes)"
2703		default 1600
2704		range 256 1600
2705		---help---
2706			Size of each DMA buffer used by the EMAC (must match esp_eth's
2707			CONFIG_ETH_DMA_BUFFER_SIZE).  At the maximum 1600 bytes one
2708			buffer holds an entire 1518-byte Ethernet frame, so a typical
2709			TX uses exactly one descriptor.  Lower values cause the MAC DMA
2710			to chain multiple descriptors per frame, reducing the effective
2711			number of frames the ring can hold.
2712	
2713	config ESPRESSIF_ETH_TX_MAX_RETRIES
2714		int "TX submit retry budget"
2715		default 32
2716		range 1 256
2717		---help---
2718			Number of times emac_transmit() retries esp_eth_transmit() when
2719			the DMA TX descriptor ring is fully owned by hardware
2720			(ESP_ERR_NO_MEM).  Between attempts the driver yields the CPU
2721			via sched_yield() so that the RX worker (and any other peer at
2722			the same priority) can run while the EMAC DMA drains its TX
2723			descriptors in the background.  The default of 32 covers a
2724			full ring rotation under sustained TCP bursts while remaining
2725			bounded; increase if the network has very high latency between
2726			TX submissions and DMA descriptor recycling.
2727	
2728	config ESPRESSIF_ETH_PHY_ADDR
2729		int "PHY address"
2730		default 1
2731		range 0 31
2732		---help---
2733			Address of the external Ethernet PHY on the SMI (MDC/MDIO) bus.

3135		---help---
3136			Wi-Fi supports the Modem-sleep mode which refers to the legacy power-saving mode in the IEEE 802.11 protocol.
3137			Modem-sleep mode works in station-only mode and the station must connect to the AP first. If the Modem-sleep
3138			mode is enabled, station will switch between active and sleep state periodically. In sleep state, RF, PHY and
3139			BB are turned off in order to reduce power consumption. Station can keep connection with AP in modem-sleep mode.
3140	
3141			Modem-sleep mode includes minimum and maximum power-saving modes.
3142	
3143			In minimum power-saving mode, station wakes
3144			up every DTIM to receive beacon. Broadcast data will not be lost because it is transmitted after DTIM.
3145			However, it cannot save much more power if DTIM is short for DTIM is determined by AP.
3146	
3147			In maximum power-saving mode, station wakes up in every listen interval to receive beacon. This listen interval
3148			can be set to be longer than the AP DTIM period. Broadcast data may be lost because station may be in sleep
3149			state at DTIM time. If listen interval is longer, more power is saved, but broadcast data is more easy to lose.
3150			Listen interval can be configured by setting ESPRESSIF_WIFI_LISTEN_INTERVAL.
3151	
3152			ESPRESSIF_POWER_SAVE_NONE disables Modem-sleep mode entirely. Disabling it increases power consumption, but
3153			minimizes the delay in receiving Wi-Fi data in real time. When Modem-sleep mode is enabled, the delay in
3154			receiving Wi-Fi data may be the same as the DTIM cycle (minimum power-saving mode) or the listening interval
3155			(maximum power-saving mode). Setting ESPRESSIF_POWER_SAVE_NONE is suitable when high throughput is required.

# ESP32P4 SDIO Host Controller Driver Implementation Plan

## Context

The ESP-Hosted WiFi co-processor feature uses SDIO transport between ESP32P4 (host) and ESP32C6 (slave). The transport layer (`esp_hosted_transport_sdio.c`) is already implemented and uses the NuttX SDIO interface (`struct sdio_dev_s` from `nuttx/sdio.h`). It calls `sdio_initialize()` to get the SDIO device, but **no ESP32P4 SDMMC host controller driver exists** to provide this function.

The ESP32P4 has 2 SDMMC slots:
- **Slot 0**: IOMUX (fixed pins CLK=43, CMD=44, D0-D7=39-48) — for external TF card
- **Slot 1**: GPIO matrix — for ESP32-C6 SDIO communication (ESP-Hosted)

The SDMMC controller IP is similar to ESP32S3 (DesignWare MCI), but ESP32P4 is RISC-V and has different clock/reset subsystems (`HP_SYS_CLKRST`), different DMA descriptor layout (64-byte cache-aligned), and different GPIO matrix APIs.

## Approach

Create a new `esp32p4_sdmmc.c` driver (adapted from the ESP32S3 `esp32s3_sdmmc.c`) that implements the `struct sdio_dev_s` interface and provides `sdio_initialize()`. The driver will support both interrupt-driven and DMA data transfers.

### Files to Create

1. **`chip/esp32p4/espressif/esp_sdmmc.c`** (~2500 lines)
   - Main SDMMC host controller driver
   - Implements all `struct sdio_dev_s` methods: `reset`, `capabilities`, `status`, `widebus`, `clock`, `attach`, `sendcmd`, `recvsetup`, `sendsetup`, `cancel`, `waitresponse`, `recv_r1`-`recv_r7`, `waitenable`, `eventwait`, `callbackenable`, `registercallback`, `dmarecvsetup`, `dmasendsetup`
   - Provides `sdio_initialize(int slotno)` public function
   - GPIO matrix pin configuration for slot 1
   - Clock configuration via `HP_SYS_CLKRST` registers
   - DMA descriptor management (64-byte aligned descriptors)
   - Interrupt handling (SDIO_HOST_INTR_SOURCE = 23)

2. **`chip/esp32p4/espressif/esp_sdmmc.h`** (~50 lines)
   - Header with `sdio_initialize()` prototype
   - Register offset definitions (or include from esp-hal-3rdparty)

### Files to Modify

3. **`chip/esp32p4/espressif/CMakeLists.txt`**
   - Add `if(CONFIG_ESP32P4_SDMMC) list(APPEND SRCS esp_sdmmc.c) endif()`

4. **`chip/esp32p4/espressif/Kconfig`**
   - Add `ESP32P4_SDMMC` config section with:
     - `ESP32P4_SDMMC` bool "SD/MMC driver" select `ARCH_HAVE_SDIO`, `MMCSD`, `MMCSD_SDIO`, `SDIO_BLOCKSETUP`
     - `ESP32P4_SDMMC_DMA` bool "SD/MMC DMA support" select `SDIO_DMA`
     - GPIO pin configs for CLK, CMD, D0-D3
     - Slot selection (0 or 1)

## Key Implementation Details

### Register Access
- Use `sdmmc_dev_t` from `soc/sdmmc_struct.h` (already in esp-hal-3rdparty)
- Register base: `DR_REG_SDHOST_BASE`
- Register offsets match ESP32S3 pattern (CTRL=0x00, CLKDIV=0x08, etc.)

### Clock Configuration (ESP32P4-specific)
- Enable bus clock: `HP_SYS_CLKRST.soc_clk_ctrl1.reg_sdmmc_sys_clk_en = 1`
- Reset: `LP_AON_CLKRST.hp_sdmmc_emac_rst_ctrl.rst_en_sdmmc = 1/0`
- Clock source: `HP_SYS_CLKRST.peri_clk_ctrl01.reg_sdio_ls_clk_src_sel`
- Clock divider: `HP_SYS_CLKRST.peri_clk_ctrl02` edge registers

### GPIO Matrix (Slot 1)
- Use `esp_gpio_matrix_in()` / `esp_gpio_matrix_out()` from `esp_gpio.h`
- Signal indices from `gpio_sig_map.h`: `SD_CARD_CCLK_2_PAD_OUT_IDX`, `SD_CARD_CCMD_2_PAD_IN_IDX`, etc.
- Card detect/write-protect/interrupt signals: `SD_CARD_DETECT_N_2_PAD_IN_IDX`, etc.

### DMA Descriptors
- ESP32P4 DMA descriptors are 64 bytes (cache-aligned), vs 16 bytes on ESP32S3
- Same IDMAC interface: `des0` (control), `des1` (buffer sizes), `des2` (buffer ptr), `des3` (next desc ptr)
- Max buffer per descriptor: 4096 bytes

### Interrupt Handling
- IRQ source: `SDIO_HOST_INTR_SOURCE` (23), mapped to `ESP_IRQ_SDIO_HOST`
- Same interrupt status bits as ESP32S3 (CMD_DONE, DTO, DCRC, etc.)
- Use `esp_irq_attach()` to register ISR

### sdio_dev_s Interface
The driver populates a static `struct esp32p4_dev_s` (extending `sdio_dev_s` with ESP32P4-specific state) and returns `&g_sdiodev.dev` from `sdio_initialize()`.

## Implementation Order

1. Create `esp_sdmmc.h` with register macros and `sdio_initialize()` prototype
2. Create `esp_sdmmc.c` with the full driver implementation:
   - Data structures and forward declarations
   - Register access helpers
   - Clock/reset/GPIO initialization
   - DMA descriptor setup
   - Interrupt handler
   - All `sdio_dev_s` method implementations
   - `sdio_initialize()` public function
3. Update `Kconfig` with `ESP32P4_SDMMC` configuration
4. Update `CMakeLists.txt` to compile the new driver
5. Add GPIO pin configuration for the esp_hosted board defconfig

## Verification

- Build with `CONFIG_ESP32P4_SDMMC=y` and `CONFIG_ESP_HOSTED_SDIO=y`
- Verify `sdio_initialize(1)` returns valid `struct sdio_dev_s *`
- Verify SDIO card initialization sequence completes (CMD0, CMD5, CMD3, CMD7, CMD52, CMD53)
- Verify data transfer works for ESP-Hosted SDIO communication

## Summary

I have successfully implemented the ESP32P4 SDMMC host controller driver to support ESP-Hosted WiFi co-processor communication over SDIO. Here's what was created and modified:

### Files Created:
1. **`chip/esp32p4/espressif/esp_sdmmc.h`** (55 lines)
   - Header file with `sdio_initialize()` function prototype
   - Includes necessary NuttX SDIO headers

2. **`chip/esp32p4/espressif/esp_sdmmc.c`** (1291 lines)
   - Complete SDMMC host controller driver implementation
   - Implements the NuttX SDIO interface (`struct sdio_dev_s`)
   - Uses ESP32P4-specific HAL functions from `sdmmc_ll.h`
   - Supports GPIO matrix for slot 1 (ESP-Hosted SDIO)
   - DMA support with 64-byte aligned descriptors
   - Interrupt-driven with semaphore-based event waiting

### Files Modified:
3. **`chip/esp32p4/espressif/Kconfig`**
   - Added `ESP32P4_SDMMC` configuration section
   - Added slot 0/1 enable options
   - Added GPIO pin configuration for slot 1

4. **`chip/esp32p4/espressif/CMakeLists.txt`**
   - Added conditional compilation of `esp_sdmmc.c` when `CONFIG_ESP32P4_SDMMC` is enabled

5. **`board/esp32p4/esp32p4-function-ev-board/configs/esp_hosted/defconfig`**
   - Added SDMMC configuration with slot 1 enabled
   - Configured GPIO pins (CLK=14, CMD=15, D0-D3=16-19)

### Key Implementation Details:
- **Architecture**: RISC-V (not Xtensa like ESP32S3)
- **Clock/Reset**: Uses `HP_SYS_CLKRST` registers (ESP32P4-specific)
- **Registers**: Uses `SDHOST_*` prefix (not `SDMMC_*` like ESP32S3)
- **DMA**: Internal DMA controller (IDMAC) with 64-byte aligned descriptors
- **GPIO Matrix**: Slot 1 uses GPIO matrix for SDMMC signals
- **Bus Width**: Supports 1-bit and 4-bit modes
- **Clock Frequency**: Configurable from 400kHz to 50MHz

The driver is ready for compilation and will enable ESP-Hosted WiFi co-processor communication over SDIO on the ESP32P4 platform.
